tagline.zh: 腎在腳底，肝往頭上衝；最後一張牌是中風
tagline.en: Kidney in the soles, liver surging up; the last card is a stroke

desc.zh: 針灸室的臟腑辨證：腰痠夜尿說腎，頭脹易怒說肝；說到一半，有一個人突然說不出話。
desc.en: Organ patterns in the needle room: an aching back and night urination speak of the kidney, a pounding head and temper of the liver; and halfway through, someone suddenly cannot find her words.

desc.zh: 血壓、留針觀察、急救車都歸你。你是第一個發現淑卿阿姨拿不穩杯子的人。
desc.en: Blood pressure, watching retained needles and the emergency trolley are yours. You are first to see Auntie Shu-ching fumble her cup.

about.zh: 用自製的「五臟撲克」教臟腑辨證，每次都輸給護理師。口頭禪：先定位，再定性。
about.en: Teaches organ patterns with a home-made “five-organ poker” deck and always loses to the nurse. Catchphrase: locate first, then characterise.

about.zh: 五臟撲克常勝軍。每個病人上床前一定量血壓，誰拜託都一樣。
about.en: Undefeated at five-organ poker. Takes everyone’s blood pressure before they lie down, no exceptions.

about.zh: 虛構教學個案。送了四十年信，現在腰痠腿軟，晚上起來好幾次。記得全鎮每一戶的門牌。
about.en: Fictional teaching case. Forty years delivering letters; now an aching back, weak legs, up several times a night. Remembers every house number in town.

role.zh: 五十八歲，傳統市場肉攤老闆
role.en: Fifty-eight, runs a market butcher stall

about.zh: 虛構教學個案。脾氣急、嗓門大，頭脹痛好幾天。降血壓藥「有時候會忘記吃」。
about.en: Fictional teaching case. Quick temper, loud voice, a pounding head for days. Sometimes “forgets” her blood-pressure pills.

about.zh: 幫媽媽顧攤。一聽到急診兩個字，刀都放下了。
about.en: Minds the stall for her mother. Drops the cleaver the moment she hears “emergency”.

about.zh: 收到病人時第一句話永遠是：最後正常是幾點？
about.en: First question on every arrival: when was she last known well?

plain.zh: 依症狀判斷病在哪個臟腑、是虛是實、偏寒偏熱，再定證名。
plain.en: Working out from symptoms which organ is affected, whether deficient or excess, cold or hot, then naming the pattern.

plain.zh: 中醫認為腎的溫煦功能不足：腰膝痠冷、怕冷、夜尿多、精神差、舌淡胖、脈沉弱。
plain.en: In TCM the kidney’s warming function fails: cold aching back and knees, chilliness, night urination, low energy, pale swollen tongue, deep weak pulse.

plain.zh: 中醫認為源於腎、是人體最根本的氣，推動全身臟腑運作。
plain.en: In TCM the most fundamental qi, rooted in the kidney, that drives every organ.

plain.zh: 寸關尺三部中最靠近手肘的位置，中醫多用來候腎。
plain.en: Of the three pulse positions, the one nearest the elbow; in TCM read for the kidney.

plain.zh: 沉而細軟無力，重按才得；中醫認為主氣血不足、陽氣虛衰。
plain.en: Deep, fine, soft and forceless, felt only on firm pressure; in TCM a sign of depleted qi and blood or failing yang.

plain.zh: 中醫認為是元陽所在之處；背上的命門穴在腰部正中，常用灸法溫腎。
plain.en: In TCM the seat of original yang; the GV4 point sits midline in the lower back and is often warmed with moxa.

plain.zh: 中醫認為肝腎陰虛、陰不制陽，肝陽往上衝：頭脹痛、眩暈、面紅目赤、急躁、耳鳴。
plain.en: In TCM, when liver and kidney yin cannot restrain yang, liver yang surges upward: pounding headache, dizziness, red face and eyes, irritability, tinnitus.

plain.zh: 五行治法：滋補腎水來涵養肝木，讓上亢的肝陽平下來。
plain.en: A five-phase method: nourish kidney water so it can hold liver wood and calm the rising yang.

plain.zh: 中醫指頭暈、肢體麻木無力、口舌歪斜、言語不利等將要中風的徵象；西醫要當急性中風處理。
plain.en: In TCM the signs before a stroke: dizziness, numb or weak limbs, a twisted mouth or tongue, faltering speech; in Western terms treat as an acute stroke.

plain.zh: 伸舌時偏向一側；中醫認為是風痰阻絡，西醫看作神經學徵象。
plain.en: The tongue veers to one side when put out; in TCM wind-phlegm blocking the channels, in Western terms a neurological sign.

plain.zh: 病人最後一次被確認沒有中風症狀的時間；決定能不能做打通血管的治療。
plain.en: The last time the patient was definitely free of stroke symptoms; it decides whether clot-busting treatment is possible.

plain.zh: 提示危險的徵象；在針灸室裡，它可能在留針的時候出現。
plain.en: A sign of danger; in the needle room it can appear while the needles are in.

text.zh: 石醫師手做的牌：每張寫一個症狀。小柔今天又贏了，用一張「舌歪」收尾。
text.en: Dr Shih’s home-made deck, a symptom on every card. Nurse Jou won again today, finishing on “deviated tongue”.

text.zh: 溫灸盒、艾條、抽煙機。腎陽虛的老人家最愛這一角，說像冬天的灶腳。
text.en: Moxa boxes, sticks and the extractor. Elderly patients with kidney yang deficiency love this corner; they say it feels like a winter kitchen hearth.

text.zh: 血壓計、血氧機、血糖機、氧氣、急救藥品。針灸室也有，因為紅旗不挑地方。
text.en: Blood-pressure cuff, oximeter, glucose meter, oxygen and emergency drugs. The needle room has one too, because red flags don’t choose their venue.

text.zh: 腎經從足底湧泉起，肝經從大腳趾起。石醫師說：兩條都從腳底往上走，所以老人家要先顧腳。
text.en: The kidney channel starts at the sole, the liver channel at the big toe. Dr Shih says: both climb from the feet, so look after an old person’s feet first.

text.zh: 先用八綱定性（表裡、寒熱、虛實、陰陽），再依各臟腑的特徵症狀定位（肺咳喘、心悸寐、脾納便、肝情志目筋、腎腰尿耳），接著辨氣血陰陽哪一項失調，找病因，最後定出證名並立治法。例如腰膝痠冷、夜尿、怕冷：定位在腎、性質虛寒，證名腎陽虛，治以溫補腎陽。
text.en: First characterise with the eight principles (exterior-interior, cold-heat, deficiency-excess, yin-yang), then locate by each organ’s signature (lung: cough; heart: palpitations, sleep; spleen: appetite, stools; liver: mood, eyes, sinews; kidney: back, urine, ears), then decide which of qi, blood, yin or yang is out of balance, find the cause, and name the pattern and method. Cold aching back and knees, night urination, chilliness: located in the kidney, deficient and cold, kidney yang deficiency, treated by warming kidney yang.

name.en: Liver and kidney share a source

text.zh: 中醫認為腎藏精、肝藏血，精血互生，稱肝腎同源。腎陰不足，水不涵木，肝陽就上亢：頭脹、眩暈、急躁、耳鳴、血壓常偏高。治法平肝潛陽兼滋腎陰，常用太衝、風池、百會，配太溪。
text.en: In TCM the kidney stores essence and the liver stores blood, and each makes the other: liver and kidney share a source. When kidney yin is low, water cannot nourish wood, and liver yang rises: pounding head, dizziness, irritability, tinnitus, often a high blood pressure. The method calms the liver, anchors yang and nourishes kidney yin, with LR3, GB20 and GV20 alongside KI3.

text.zh: 臉歪、手腳無力或麻、說話不清、舌歪、突然視力模糊或劇烈頭痛，就是急性中風直到證明不是。立刻停止所有處置、出針、記下最後正常時間、量血壓與血糖、不給任何東西吃喝、叫救護車。能不能打通血管，看時間。中醫的中風先兆概念很早就提醒了這一刻。
text.en: A drooping face, a weak or numb arm or leg, slurred speech, a deviated tongue, sudden loss of vision or a thunderclap headache is an acute stroke until proven otherwise. Stop everything, remove needles, note when she was last known well, check blood pressure and glucose, give nothing by mouth, call an ambulance. Whether the clot can be cleared depends on time. TCM’s idea of a stroke warning has pointed at this moment for centuries.

name.en: Kidney yang versus kidney yin deficiency

text.zh: 兩者都有腰痠、耳鳴、夜尿。腎陽虛偏寒：怕冷、手腳冰、尿清長、舌淡胖、脈沉弱，治以溫補腎陽，代表方腎氣丸。腎陰虛偏熱：潮熱盜汗、口乾、手足心熱、舌紅少苔、脈細數，代表方六味地黃丸。中醫認為陰陽互根，久病常陰陽兩虛。
text.en: Both bring an aching back, tinnitus and night urination. Kidney yang deficiency runs cold: chilly, cold hands and feet, copious clear urine, pale swollen tongue, deep weak pulse; warm kidney yang, with Shen Qi Wan. Kidney yin deficiency runs hot: hot flushes, night sweats, dry mouth, hot palms and soles, red tongue with scant coat, thready rapid pulse; Liu Wei Di Huang Wan. In TCM yin and yang root each other, and long illness often depletes both.

lines.zh: 石醫師在白板前發牌。每張牌寫著一個症狀。小柔已經贏了兩局。
lines.en: Dr Shih deals cards at the board, a symptom on each. Nurse Jou has already won two hands.

lines.zh: 「夜尿」「腰痠」「耳鳴」，這手牌是哪一臟？
lines.en: “Night urination”, “aching back”, “tinnitus”: which organ holds this hand?

lines.zh: 腎。
lines.en: Kidney.

lines.zh: 對。臟腑辨證有順序，排給我看，別再讓小柔贏了。
lines.en: Right. Organ pattern identification has an order. Lay it out, and stop letting Jou win.

steps.en: Eight principles: cold, heat, deficiency, excess
Locate the organ by its signature
Which of qi, blood, yin, yang

post.zh: 還有第零步：上床前量血壓。
post.en: And step zero: blood pressure before anyone lies down.

note.en: Back, night urine, cold: kidney yang

guide.en: Settle Uncle Chin-tsai on couch one

lines.zh: 送信送了四十年，現在腰痠腿軟。晚上起來尿三四次，膝蓋冷得像冰箱。
lines.en: Forty years of letters, and now my back aches and my legs are weak. Up three or four times a night, knees cold as a fridge.

lines.zh: 尿的顏色？小便會不會很細、很難解？有沒有發燒、背痛到半夜痛醒、體重掉？
lines.en: What colour is the urine? Is the stream weak or hard to start? Any fever, back pain that wakes you, weight loss?

lines.zh: 清清的，量很多。泌尿科看過，攝護腺說還好。沒發燒，體重沒變。
lines.en: Clear, lots of it. The urologist checked my prostate; said it’s fine. No fever, same weight.

lines.zh: 紅旗問過了。定位：腎。定性呢？
lines.en: Red flags asked. Location: kidney. Character?

post.zh: 怕冷、尿清長、膝冷：虛寒。腎陽虛，元氣的根不夠溫。
post.en: Chilly, copious clear urine, cold knees: deficiency-cold. Kidney yang deficiency; the root of original qi isn’t warm enough.

lines.zh: 三指放好。腎看哪一部？
lines.en: Three fingers on. Which position is the kidney?

post.zh: 尺部。兩手的尺脈都沉，要壓到底才有，軟軟細細的。
post.en: The chi position. Both chi pulses are deep, only at the bottom, soft and fine.

lines.zh: 沉而細軟，重按才得，指下沒什麼力。
lines.en: Deep, fine and soft, found only on firm pressure, with little force under the fingers.

q.zh: 沉細軟而無力，尺部尤甚。這是什麼脈？
q.en: Deep, fine, soft and forceless, most at chi. Which pulse?

options.zh: 弱脈：陽氣虛衰，腎陽不足
options.en: Weak: failing yang, kidney yang short

why.zh: 中醫認為弱脈沉細無力，主陽氣虛衰、氣血不足；尺部尤甚，指向腎。
why.en: In TCM the weak pulse is deep, fine and forceless, a sign of failing yang and depleted qi and blood; worst at chi, it points to the kidney.

why.zh: 弦脈端直有力；這條脈軟得幾乎沒有力。
why.en: Wiry is straight and strong; this one is soft, almost without force.

why.zh: 洪脈輕取就滿指；這條要壓到底。
why.en: Surging floods at a touch; this one hides at the bottom.

lines.zh: 溫補腎陽的代表方是腎氣丸。它不是只放熱藥，你看看。
lines.en: The classic for warming kidney yang is Shen Qi Wan. It isn’t only hot herbs; look.

q.en: Select herbs of Shen Qi Wan

post.zh: 大部分是滋陰的藥，只有附子、桂枝是溫陽的。
post.en: Most of them nourish yin; only aconite and cinnamon twig warm yang.

post.zh: 陰中求陽，微微生火。陰陽互根。附子有毒，用炮製品、先煎、依處方。
post.en: Seek yang within yin, a small flame. Yin and yang root each other. Aconite is toxic: processed, decocted first, per prescription.

post.zh: 小柔把溫灸盒放上命門和腎俞。進財伯說：像冬天坐在灶腳。
post.en: Nurse Jou sets a moxa box over GV4, the gate of life, and BL23. Uncle Chin-tsai says it feels like sitting by a winter hearth.

note.zh: 頭脹、面紅、急躁：肝陽上亢
note.en: Pounding head, red face: liver yang rising

lines.zh: 頭脹好幾天了，像戴了一頂太小的安全帽！耳朵嗡嗡叫，看誰都不順眼！
lines.en: My head’s been pounding for days, like a helmet two sizes too small! My ears buzz and everyone annoys me!

lines.zh: 降血壓藥有在吃嗎？
lines.en: Are you taking your blood-pressure pills?

lines.zh: 有時候會忘記啦，攤子忙。
lines.en: Sometimes I forget. The stall’s busy.

q.zh: 淑卿阿姨頭脹、面紅、忘了吃降壓藥。下針前你要？
q.en: Pounding head, red face, missed BP pills. Before the needles, you…

options.zh: 先量血壓、問神經症狀，再請醫師決定
options.en: Take BP, ask neuro symptoms, then the doctor decides

why.zh: 頭痛加漏吃降壓藥，先量血壓並問手腳麻、無力、說話、視力。有基準值，之後才知道變化。
why.en: Headache with missed BP pills: measure first and ask about numbness, weakness, speech and vision. Without a baseline you can’t see a change later.

options.zh: 直接扎太衝平肝，針會降壓
options.en: Needle LR3 now; needles lower BP

why.zh: 沒有量就不知道多高，也不知道等一下變了多少。
why.en: Unmeasured, you don’t know how high it is or how much it changes later.

options.en: Moxa GV20 to relax her first

why.zh: 中醫認為肝陽上亢不宜溫灸頭頂，像往上衝的火再加熱。
why.en: In TCM rising liver yang is not warmed at the crown; it adds heat to a flame already climbing.

lines.zh: 血壓很高。手腳有力、講話清楚、視力正常。我已經通知石醫師，十五分鐘後複測。
lines.en: Blood pressure is high. Limbs strong, speech clear, vision normal. Dr Shih is informed; I’ll repeat it shortly.

lines.zh: 先吃她帶在包包裡的降壓藥。針只扎輕的，留針時你一直在旁邊。
lines.en: Have her take the pill in her handbag. Light needling only, and you stay beside her while the needles are in.

lines.zh: 肝陽上亢：平肝一個、頭部兩個、滋腎一個。滋水涵木。
lines.en: Ascendant liver yang: one to calm the liver, two on the head, one to nourish the kidney. Water nourishing wood.

q.zh: 指出太衝、風池、百會、太溪
q.en: Point out LR3, GB20, GV20 and KI3

post.zh: 風池朝鼻尖方向，不可往上內深刺。
post.en: GB20 angled toward the nose tip, never deep upward and inward.

post.zh: 腎水不足，肝木就往上衝。五行不是背的，是看的。
post.en: When kidney water runs low, liver wood surges up. The five phases aren’t recited; they’re observed.

guide.en: Revise yin failing to restrain yang

lines.zh: 陰陽的對立制約，在她身上長什麼樣子？
lines.en: What does the mutual restraint of yin and yang look like in her?

post.zh: 肝腎的陰不夠，管不住陽，陽就往上衝：頭脹、面紅、耳鳴、急躁。
post.en: Liver and kidney yin are too weak to hold yang back, so it surges: pounding head, red face, tinnitus, temper.

lines.zh: 鏘一聲。淑卿阿姨右手的水杯掉在地上。
lines.en: A clatter. The cup has fallen from Auntie Shu-ching’s right hand.

lines.zh: 我……手……怎麼……拿不……
lines.en: My… hand… why can’t… hold…

lines.zh: 阿姨，笑一個給我看。右邊嘴角掉下來了。現在十點四十二分，我記下來了。
lines.en: Auntie, give me a smile. The right side of her mouth droops. It’s 10:42; I’ve written it down.

lines.zh: 舌頭伸出來。
lines.en: Put out your tongue.

q.zh: 伸舌偏向一側、舌紅苔黃。在此刻代表什麼？
q.en: Tongue veers to one side, red with yellow coat. What does it mean now?

options.zh: 中風先兆：當急性中風處理，立即急救
options.en: Stroke warning: treat as acute stroke now

why.zh: 中醫認為舌歪、語言不利、肢體無力是風痰阻絡的中風之兆；西醫上這是急性中風的神經學徵象，每一分鐘都算數。
why.en: In TCM a deviated tongue, faltering speech and a weak limb are wind-phlegm blocking the channels, a stroke sign; in Western terms they are neurological signs of acute stroke, and every minute counts.

options.en: Liver fire: add needles to clear it

why.zh: 舌紅苔黃是肝火沒錯，但歪斜的舌頭在喊救命。
why.en: The red tongue and yellow coat are liver fire, true, but the deviated tongue is crying for help.

options.en: Her tongue is tired from lying down

why.zh: 舌頭不會因為躺著而歪。這是神經的問題。
why.en: Lying down doesn’t make a tongue veer. This is the nervous system.

lines.zh: 血壓計又響了：比剛剛更高。她的右手抬不起來。
lines.en: The cuff alarms again: higher than before. She can’t lift her right arm.

options.zh: 全部出針、記時間、測血糖、禁食、叫救護車
options.en: All needles out, note time, check glucose, nothing by mouth, ambulance

why.zh: 疑似急性中風：停止處置、出針、記下最後正常時間、量血糖排除低血糖、不給吃喝、叫救護車。不要在診所自行把血壓壓下來。
why.en: Suspected acute stroke: stop, remove needles, note the last-known-well time, check glucose to exclude a low sugar, nothing by mouth, ambulance. Don’t try to force the pressure down in the clinic.

options.en: Prick the finger tips to lower the pressure

why.zh: 放血救急是古書的方法，今天的急救是時間與血管。先叫救護車。
why.en: Bloodletting is the old texts’ emergency; today’s emergency is time and the vessel. Ambulance first.

options.zh: 讓她坐起來喝點水休息
options.en: Sit her up with some water to rest

why.zh: 中風的人吞嚥可能有問題，喝水會嗆到肺。
why.en: After a stroke swallowing may fail; water could go into the lungs.

post.zh: 針全部出了，數量對。血糖正常，不是低血糖。救護車在路上。
post.en: All needles out, count correct. Glucose normal, not a low sugar. Ambulance on its way.

post.zh: 十點半我替她複測血壓時，她還會跟我吵。
post.en: At half past ten, when I rechecked her pressure, she was still arguing with me.

lines.zh: 急救車上的東西都在嗎？救護員到了要交什麼？
lines.en: Is everything on the trolley? What do we hand the paramedics?

q.zh: 在急救車上找出血糖機與血氧機
q.en: Find the glucose meter and oximeter on the trolley

post.zh: 交接：最後正常時間十點半、症狀十點四十二分、血壓、血糖、漏吃降壓藥、針已全部移除。
post.en: Handover: last known well half past ten, symptoms at 10:42, blood pressure, glucose, missed pills, all needles removed.

lines.zh: 救護員問：上針之前血壓多少？
lines.en: The paramedic asks: what was her pressure before the needles?

lines.zh: ……沒有量。
lines.en: …We didn’t take it.

lines.zh: 小柔說的第零步，就是為了這個問題。下次每一個病人都要有基準值。
lines.en: Jou’s step zero exists for exactly this question. From now on, every patient has a baseline.

lines.zh: 我媽怎麼了？她早上還在攤子罵客人！
lines.en: What’s happened? This morning she was shouting at customers!

lines.zh: 她在針灸時出現中風的症狀，救護車送去急診了。我們有記下時間，這很重要。請帶她的藥袋過去。
lines.en: She showed stroke symptoms during treatment and the ambulance has taken her to the ER. We noted the time, which matters a lot. Please bring her medicine bag.

lines.zh: 我現在就去。刀我放下了。
lines.en: I’m going now. I’ve put the cleaver down.

lines.zh: 腦血管阻塞，在時間內打通了。你們記的最後正常時間很準，幫了大忙。右手已經會動了。
lines.en: A blocked vessel, opened in time. Your last-known-well time was spot on and made all the difference. Her right hand is already moving.

lines.zh: 之後的降壓藥一定要天天吃。中醫要調理可以，先讓我們知道。
lines.en: From now on the BP pills are every day. TCM care is welcome later; just keep us informed.

lines.zh: 時間就是腦。今天那幾分鐘，比我們任何一根針都有用。
lines.en: Time is brain. Those minutes today did more than any needle of ours.

note.en: Locate, characterise, and save life first

lines.zh: 今天兩手牌。進財伯是腎，虛寒，溫補就好。淑卿阿姨是肝，可是那手牌最後一張是中風。
lines.en: Two hands today. Uncle Chin-tsai was kidney, deficient and cold; warm and tonify. Auntie Shu-ching was liver, but the last card in her hand was a stroke.

lines.zh: 臟腑辨證教你看得懂病人，紅旗教你知道什麼時候放下牌。
lines.en: Organ patterns teach you to read a patient; red flags teach you when to put the cards down.

lines.zh: 最後一局我又贏了。「舌歪」那張。
lines.en: I won the last hand again. The “deviated tongue” card.

lines.zh: 這局，你贏得好。
lines.en: That one you won well.

lines.zh: 我媽想跟你們說：她今天晚上自己拿杯子喝水了，沒有掉。還有，她說以後降壓藥會天天吃。
lines.en: Mum wants you to know: tonight she held a cup and drank by herself, and didn’t drop it. And she says she’ll take her BP pills every day from now on.

lines.zh: 她說是那個護理師先叫她笑的。
lines.en: She says it was the nurse who asked her to smile first.

lines.zh: 你在筆記本上畫了兩張牌：一張「腎陽虛」，一張「舌歪」。
lines.en: In your notebook you draw two cards: “kidney yang deficiency” and “deviated tongue”.

lines.zh: 第二張，你畫得特別大。
lines.en: The second one you draw extra large.

sub.zh: 先定位，再定性；紅旗一出，先放下牌
sub.en: Locate, then characterise; at a red flag, put the cards down
